2. The appeal is found to be out of time by 45 days in view of the fact that the impugned judgment and order was pronounced on 13-5- 84 and that the application for its certified copy was filed on 4-6-84 and certified copy was made ready on 10-6-84 on which date the complainant also obtained it but filed the appeal in this Court on 4-9-84. The appellant filed an application for condonation of delay. The limitation in the present case is 60 days as prescribed by section 417(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure which reads as follows :- 

 No provision has been made by the Code of Criminal Procedure, by which the aforesaid limitation of sixty days is prescribed, for condonation of delay. The learned Advocate for the appellant submits that the delay may be condoned under section 5 of the Limitation Act. 

 Section 5 of the Limitation Act reads as follows: 

 "5. Any appeal or application for a revision or a review of judgment or far leave to appeal or any other application to which this section is made applicable by or under any enactment for the time being in force may be admitted after the period of limitation prescribed thereof, when the appellant or applicant satisfies the Court that he had sufficient cause for not preferring the appeal or making the application within such period." 

 In order to decide whether this section is applicable to the present case it is necessary to read it with section 29(2) of the Limitation Act which reads as follows :- 

 "29(2). Where any special law prescribes for any suit; appeal or application a period of limitation different from the period prescribed thereof by first schedule, the provisions of section 3 shall apply, as if such period were prescribed thereof in that schedule and for the purpose of determining any period of limitation prescribed for any suit, appeal or application by any special law 

 3. It is now well settled that generally on a question of limitation the Limitation Act is the general law and all other Acts in so far as they deal with the question of limitation are special laws. The Code of Criminal Procedure is a general law relating to procedure, but it is a special law while prescribing a limitation for a particular purpose. Section 417(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, therefore, is a special law prescribing a limitation for filing an appeal from an order of acquittal under section 417(2) of the same Code different from that prescribed by the Limitation Act, as Article 157 of the Limitation Act prescribes limitation of a period of six months for filing and appeal against an order of acquittal under the Code of Criminal Procedure. It may be, mentioned that before section 417(2) was inserted in the said Code by the Amending Ordinance No. 49 of 1978, the Government only was given the right of appeal against an order of acquittal under section 417 of the said Code (now re-numbered as 417(1) and obviously the said limitation for a period of six months is meant for such appeal to the High Court Division by the Government against an order of acquittal passed by any Court. 

 4. By inserting section 417(2) in the Code of Criminal Procedure by an amendment under the Law Reforms Ordinance, 1978 (Ordinance No. 49 of 1978) a complainant in any case instituted upon complaint only has been given a right of appeal to the High Court Division from an order of acquittal on any ground which involves a matter of law only prescribing a special period of limitation under section 417(3) of the same Code different from the period prescribed by the first schedule of the limitation Act. In this view of the matter section 29 (2) (a) of the Limitation Act is attracted in the present case and consequently in computing the period of limitation in respect of an appeal under section 417(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure the time required for obtaining a copy of the judgment and order appealed from, the day of pronouncement of judgment, etc. shall be excluded as provided in sections 9 and 12 of the Limitation Act and when the period of limitation expires on a day when the Court is closed, the appeal under section 417(2) CrPC may be filed on the day the Court reopens as provided in section 4 of the Limitation Act. In view of the provisions of section 29(2)(b) that the remaining provisions of the Limitation Act shall not apply, section 5 of the said Act has no application to an appeal under section 417(2) CrPC. The said provision of section 5 of the Limitation Act has not be made applicable to an appeal by a complainant in a complaint case under section 417 (2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure by or under any other enactment also.
